title: Customer-facing billing attribution job: aggregate token events into invoice-ready ledger rows
creator: Maya Patel
description: Implement a durable aggregation job that consumes token-level events and emits invoice-ready ledger rows attributed to customer accounts, projects, and API routes. The job must support strong idempotency, deterministic attribution, late-arriving events handling, and daily reconciliation against the primary billing ledger (Postgres). This work spans the streaming consumer, transformation logic, dedupe/aggregation store, and downstream export to the billing service. It is intended to replace the brittle nightly script currently used for edge-case corrections and to provide near-real-time cost visibility in the Console.
acceptance_criteria: Aggregations produce one ledger row per (customer_id, route_id, day, model_variant, price_tier) with token counts aligned to the billing pricing rules
Pipeline guarantees exactly-once semantics for events with globally unique event_id and supports at-least-once ingestion from Kafka without duplicating billed tokens
Late-arriving events up to the 72-hour window are folded into the appropriate day with an audit flag; beyond 72 hours, events route to a manual correction queue
Daily automated reconciliation job reports <0.1% unexplained token delta between aggregation output and source token stream for the previous 7 days
Console displays per-customer attribution with sub-minute freshness for recent activity and shows an explicit reconciliation status for each billing day
comments: 2026-02-25 - Maya Patel: Kickoff — outlined scope and measurement goals. Preferred approach: hybrid streaming + micro-batch for reconciliation. Raised question about whether to use Beam on Dataflow vs Flink on K8s; deferred to infra decision.

2026-03-02 - Ethan Liu: Spike complete. Implemented local prototype using Kafka consumer + incremental write to ClickHouse as aggregation store. Pros: fast rollups, good query latency. Cons: ClickHouse TTL semantics complicate idempotent updates for late arrivals. Documented patch approaches in design doc.

2026-03-05 - SRE (Priya Rao): Concern about cross-account encryption keys when exporting final ledger rows to Postgres in customer-managed private deployments. Blocking until RBAC/KMS patterns are validated. Opening ENG-9480 to track KMS gating work.

2026-03-07 - Data Eng (Liam O'Connor): Recommendation to move dedupe and windowing into the stream layer using exactly-once sinks (Kafka transactions) and treat ClickHouse as read-optimized. This reduces correctness obligations on downstream tasks. Weighed trade-offs — slight increase in latency vs stronger correctness guarantees.

2026-03-10 - Ethan Liu: Decided to adopt a two-path architecture: (1) real-time attribution via a Kafka consumer that writes incremental deltas to an append-only S3 path (parquet) partitioned by day and customer for quick Console reads, (2) nightly reconciliation job (Airflow-managed Spark job) that compacts S3 deltas into canonical ledger rows and writes to Postgres. Implemented PR#4123 to add transactional write markers and event_id dedupe table. Follow-up tasks: finalize encryption flow, add SLO alerts, and create migration playbook.
implementation_notes: Key components: Kafka consumer with watermarking and event dedupe (event_id + ingestion_ts), append-only S3 staging, Spark compaction job that applies pricing rules and merges deltas into canonical ledger rows, final write to Postgres using upsert with ledger_version. Important: tag reconciled rows with reconciliation_run_id for auditability. Metrics to emit: reconciliation_success_rate, time_to_reconciliation_minutes, percent_late_tokens, unattributed_token_rate, attribution_latency_seconds.
next_steps: Complete KMS/RBAC validation with Security team (ENG-9480)
Add SLO alerting queries to Console (SLO: reconciliation_success_rate >= 99.9%)
Wire up PR#4123 into staging and run full synthetic replay for 30 days of events
Create migration plan to switch Console reads from old nightly script to new compacted ledger (include feature flag)
Author customer-facing note and billing FAQ for handling late adjustments
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Late-arriving events could cause retroactive billing changes causing customer confusion. Mitigation: expose reconciliation status and a clear adjustments log in Console; limit automatic retro-billing to 72-hour window, route older adjustments to manual review.
Risk: Duplicate events from upstream producers. Mitigation: implement event_id dedupe store and idempotent upserts; add end-to-end test harness that injects duplicate events.
Risk: High cardinality leads to large compaction jobs. Mitigation: pre-aggregate by price_tier and route_id at ingestion, and shard jobs by customer slices.
